scope: Our versioned graph format: 27 block types, typed wiring, engineering units, revisions, validation and undo/redo.
Local browser GUI with block palette, wiring, properties, templates, zoom, minimap, multi-selection, group movement/alignment, internal-wire copy/paste/duplication, grouped delete and undo.

Typed single-output definitions with required named inputs; nested reusable libraries, independent instance state, graphical definition editing with apply/discard and draft recovery, deterministic bounded expansion, portable dependency-closed library exchange and guarded deletion. Root I/O stays external. Original hierarchy persists through JSON/ST/PLCopen/GraphML/native bundle re-import. Physical terminal bindings remain outside definitions.

feature: Persistent simulation trends and alarm lifecycle
scope: Opt-in successful-scan recording with simulation/receipt timestamps, types, quality and units in bounded SQLite retention. Alarm activation/return/acknowledgment/reactivation, operator notes, event queries, source filters, paged trend CSV and resolved-source retirement. Recording failures are distinguished from executed scans. Explicit source ending closes abandoned simulation alarms with a distinct source-ended event; acknowledgment precedes retirement. Separate services provide field acquisition and optional webhook delivery. Persisted logical store identity and source kind survive complete workspace copies.

Explicitly enabled HTTP(S) routes deliver recorded simulation alarm events through a bounded durable SQLite outbox. Original source/time evidence, stable idempotency keys, payload hashes, per-route ordering, bounded backoff and retention/capacity gaps remain visible. Ambiguous sends require operator retry or discard; receipts do not acknowledge alarms or prove human receipt. Routes restart disabled. URL/bearer environment references keep secrets out of persisted configuration and logs; redirects and environment proxies are disabled. Actual loopback receivers, cross-process crash recovery and storage faults are tested. No native controller alarm acquisition, email or exactly-once guarantee.

Explicit polling jobs share an already connected BACnet/IP, BBMD foreign-device, routed or direct MS/TP interface. Finite values persist with acquisition/receipt UTC timestamps, unit labels and unknown quality unless reliability/status/out-of-service checks validate. Failures produce durable events without synthetic values; interface changes stop jobs. Separate field/simulation databases enforce source-kind identity. Jobs do not resume on restart. No point writes or native alarms. Existing Trend Log history has a separate explicit retrieval/capture service.

Explicit bounded forward ReadRange through the connected interface; standard single-value Trend Log only. Device timezone/fold, original local clocks, unresolved UTC, all 11 datum alternatives, quality, sequence gaps/wrap and partial failures stay visible. Immutable sealed captures and JSON/CSV retain provenance. No auto-connect, background polling, device writes, physical-device validation or proprietary history import.

Deterministic scans, feedback memory, PI, timers, calendar schedules with IANA zones/DST/dated exceptions, fault injection, timed scenarios and CSV traces. Explicit UTC clock injection. This is our graph runtime, not JCI firmware emulation.

2–16 graph instances with a common clock and typed/unit-checked previous-cycle links. All programs commit together; a failed cycle holds every state/output. Bounded sessions/history, quality fault records and portable workspace save/reopen. No field interfaces or equipment/firmware emulation.

Force any core graph block output, retain underlying block state, release individual/all overrides and record computed/forced values. Source faults still fail scans. Timed scenarios replay force maps; CSV includes override evidence. These holds are not exported as controller logic or sent to field devices.
Direct and transitive sources/consumers, affected outputs, previous-scan feedback boundaries, execution-order problems and click-through navigation for the portable core graph.

BMS JSON, IEC Structured Text, PLCopen TC6 XML with ST, GraphML, native Sedona bundles/SAX/SAB/SCode, a 20-kind native Niagara BOG profile and Temco Control Basic. Studio files verify original source consistency; supported foreign subsets convert with execution-difference reports. Generated ST independently compiles and runs through MatIEC/native C locally; physical PLC and Niagara runtime acceptance remain unverified.
Observed ZIP/XML containers: preserve all unknown data, jobInfo and simulationProperty entries; readable attribute/class dictionaries; original byte-exact export.

Offline exact object/record comparison with categories, bounded previews, source/full-record hashes, filters, pagination and JSON export. Application/simulation values, wiring/order, opaque metadata, comments/PIs and referenced QName bindings stay visible. Originals unchanged; no native compilation, retargeting, firmware compatibility or device write.

Studio-generated ST passes unchanged through pinned MatIEC to C and a separate native Clang process. All 27 blocks/nine examples, retained state, quality faults, timed events, calendars, macros and float32 overflow differences have independent execution tests. Host-only memory I/O; no PLC runtime certification or controller deployment.

Offline inspection of observed manufacturer Interface XML: point types, imperial/metric ranges, BACnet identities, aliases and presets. Validated selections and source-hashed migration reports distinguish rebinding/parameter/interface changes. Exact XML export preserves unknown metadata. This does not allocate CAF objects or compile/download a controller program.

Narrow offline scalar patches plus observed native block/wire/order/position inspection, guarded rewires and prototype-checked added connections between existing blocks. Exact old tuple/count, opaque native configuration, proven ports, unused destinations and execution ordering are checked. New block identities, complete application semantics, target compilation and native validation remain pending.

Source-hashed portable profiles inspect all observed saved simulation records and edit existing supported native float/Boolean startup values into a separate CAF copy. Enum, unknown and unsupported records remain read-only; ordinary properties and opaque metadata are preserved. Exact record identities, finite float32 bounds and unchanged-profile byte identity are checked against authorized samples. The workspace retains drafts and guards pending downloads. No JCI logic execution, new native block creation or vendor reopen/simulation acceptance is established.

Native Sedona compilation/execution, native Temco Control Basic compiler/interpreter host and 20 Niagara BOG graph-kind mappings are available. New JCI CAF/CAP, ALC equipment and Honeywell Spyder encoders still require verified semantics, compilers/packages and target tests. Native archive inspection, saved CAF simulation-value editing and supported conversion profiles do not establish proprietary controller compilation or deployment.

Pinned upstream compiler creates real kits, SAX, SAB and 64-bit simulator SCode. All 27 graph blocks run in a separate native VM, compared with the graph engine. Native online components/wiring persist through revisions and exports. Exported applications scan automatically; calendar/I/O mapping is a destination-runtime responsibility. Experimental local Unix port, not physical-platform certification.

All 27 blocks compile into real manufacturer bytecode and execute in the pinned interpreter host, with retained state and visible fixed-point differences. Separate native BACnet slot transfer stops, backs up, replaces, reads back and conditionally resumes an exact pinned device/slot. Real UDP/routed emulator and recovery tests pass; physical execution, flash persistence and scan cadence remain unverified. Transfer refuses unprovisioned calendars and VARs beyond 128.

20 graph kinds map to real bajaObjectGraph ZIP/XML, including Clamp, clamped/extrapolating Scale and absolute-temperature Convert. Supported foreign Reset, explicit temperature-unit converters and primitive components convert with mandatory event/status/priority review. Composite mappings preserve units, bounds and reversed endpoint meaning. Genuine manufacturer module/API metadata verifies native classes, inherited slots, link types, serialized units and palette aliases. Unknown logic/resources/configuration fail conversion; original archive bytes are preserved separately. No licensed Workbench/station execution or full station conversion.

Explicit unicast discovery, object/property reads, bounded object lists, command previews, priority-slot checks, verified writes, relinquish and durable command recovery. Optional foreign-device registration adds BBMD broadcast discovery while preserving addressed point services. Independently authored raw UDP peers and real loopback applications exercise protocol traffic. Physical controller acceptance remains unverified.

Explicit registration with an existing BBMD, exact-source acknowledgments, managed renewal, bounded lease/grace tracking, dead-link health and best-effort TTL-zero deregistration. Explicit bounded broadcast Who-Is preserves original forwarded source addresses. Failed registration/lease requires reconnect, and exact interface/BBMD settings remain bound to owned command recovery. Independently authored raw loopback BVLC peers exercise real wire requests, source checks, discovery, renewal, actual expiry, teardown and recovery. No BBMD hosting/configuration, BACnet/SC, IPv6 BVLL, NAT traversal or physical BBMD verification.

Explicit router IP plus DNET/MAC addressing. NPDU routing is exercised through an IP-to-virtual-data-link test. The approved Tailscale subnet route now permits real unicast BACnet discovery and device metadata reads from both E2/F2 NAEs. Desktop credentials remain unread; web authentication and device writes were not attempted. Downstream physical MS/TP VAV routing and native application acceptance remain unverified.

BACnet/IP, optional IPv4 BBMD foreign-device registration, direct serial legacy MS/TP master, Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU with enumerated serial interfaces. Real UDP/TCP and test-owned OS pseudoterminals verify framed point services. Physical USB/RS485 hardware remains untested. Bluetooth is excluded from the current verification scope.

Direct legacy MS/TP token master, CRC/frame decoder, bounded pyserial worker and BACpypes3 integration are implemented and exercised through real pseudoterminals. Physical bus timing and adapters remain unverified. BTCVT Bluetooth host protocol and extended/COBS frames are not implemented. Bluetooth configuration is excluded from the requested verification pass; the original BTCVT implementation requirement remains incomplete.

Graph replacement with state retention and rollback in our sandbox. Real Sox add/write/link/unlink/delete in an owned native SVM; shadow-VM preflight, configuration conflict checks, compensating rollback, persistent project save/export and value/link readback. Proprietary controller application changes remain pending. Temco slot replacement/restore uses actual private-transfer bytes, durable backup/intent and readback, with compensating recovery; it stops the slot and is not an atomic online edit. Physical hardware remains unverified.

The approved Tailscale subnet route reaches both NAEs, and actual read-only BACnet discovery/device metadata reads succeeded. Desktop credentials remain unread; web authentication and controller writes were not attempted. The physical sensor test still requires a verified native application adapter, exact target/unused terminal, original backup and verified restoration. Standard point commands cannot allocate a new native input.
Nine illustrative VAV graph examples include six FX/Metasys profiles. They are not certified Title 24 sequences or downloadable native CAFs.
Vendor manuals, source repository inventory, page-level evidence, feature requirements and explicit support gaps. Copyrighted reference PDFs and site files stay outside the code repository.
